answer: The well is only as deep as the rope that reaches the water, and the rope is measured by the man who dug it. Proof of stonemason arch via keystone measure measures the rope: an arch the mason sets only after the keystone measures 11 hands wide, cut by the master himself. The velvet is the knot at the top, tied when the digging began; the dune is the knot at the bottom, tied when the water came. Faking the depth takes a cheat 37 false knots and 37 false ropes, and the vault still comes up dry.
